# polyhedra.library: ChamferFaceOfEdge

```plato

    // The hexagon straddling an edge: endpoint, the two shrunk points of the
    // face on the far side, the other endpoint, then the two of the near face.
    // The far side is traversed first for the same winding reason as `Join`.
    // Precondition: `corner` is canonical.
    ChamferFaceOfEdge(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
    {
        var twin = self.TwinCorner(corner);
        return [self.ChamferSeedVertex(self.CornerVertex(corner)),
                VertexIndex(self.NextCorner(twin).Value),
                VertexIndex(twin.Value),
                self.ChamferSeedVertex(self.CornerDestination(corner)),
                VertexIndex(self.NextCorner(corner).Value),
                VertexIndex(corner.Value)];
    }

    // Chamfer (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamfer_(geometry)): every edge is
    // replaced by a hexagon and every original face survives as a shrunk copy of
    // itself, in its own plane. cC is the chamfered cube; iterating it is the
    // usual route to a Goldberg polyhedron.
    // V' = V + C, E' = 4E, F' = F + E.
    Chamfer(self: PolygonMesh3D, shrink: Number): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            self.ChamferVertices(shrink),
            Concatenate(
                self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => self.MovedFaceOfFace(f)),
                self.EdgeStitchFaces((m, c) => [m.ChamferFaceOfEdge(c)])));

    //==
    // Propeller.

    // The one-third points along every directed edge, then the original
    // vertices. The corner block leads, so `MovedFaceOfFace` names the rotated
    // inner copy of a face without any adjustment.
    PropellerVertices(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<Point3D>
        => Concatenate(self.TruncationPoints, self.Positions);

    // The quad between the inner copy and the boundary at one corner: this
    // corner's one-third point, the two-thirds point of the same edge (its
    // twin's), the vertex the corner points at, and the next corner's
    // one-third point.
    PropellerFaceOfCorner(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [VertexIndex(corner.Value),
            VertexIndex(self.TwinCorner(corner).Value),
            VertexIndex(self.CornerCount + self.CornerDestination(corner).Value),
            VertexIndex(self.NextCorner(corner).Value)];

    // Propeller (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation):
    // each face keeps a rotated copy of itself and the ring left over is filled
    // by one quadrilateral per corner — four blades around each face, which is
    // the name. Chiral; `Reflect` gives the other hand.
    // V' = V + C, E' = 5E, F' = F + C.
    Propeller(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            self.PropellerVertices,
            Concatenate(
                self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => self.MovedFaceOfFace(f)),
                self.CornerCount.MapRange(c => self.PropellerFaceOfCorner(CornerIndex(c)))));

    //==
    // Zip and reflect.

    // Zip (bitruncation): the Conway identity z = dk, which is truncate of the
    // dual. zC is the truncated octahedron, where tC is the truncated cube — the
    // two differ because zip cuts the DUAL's corners, not the seed's.
    // Precondition, inherited from `Dual`: no face plane passes through the origin.
    // V' = C, E' = 3E, F' = V + F.
    Zip(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => self.Dual.Truncate;

    // A face loop taken backwards: the winding fix a mirror needs, since
    // negating one coordinate reverses handedness and would otherwise turn every
    // face inside out.
    ReversedFace(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Array<VertexIndex>
        => self.FaceArity(face).MapRange(slot =>
            self.Faces.Row(face)[self.FaceArity(face) - 1 - slot]);

    // Reflect (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirality_(mathematics)): the mirror
    // image through the yz plane, with every face loop reversed so the result is
    // still wound counter-clockwise seen from outside. Identity on an achiral
    // solid up to a rotation; on snub, gyro or propeller it is the other
    // enantiomer. V, E and F are unchanged.
    Reflect(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            self.Positions.Map(p => Point3D(-p.X, p.Y, p.Z)),
            self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => self.ReversedFace(f)));

    //==
    // # Reading a polyhedron
    //
    // The measurements a Conway program is judged by. Every one is a fold over
    // the face or corner numbering, so they hold for any closed polygon mesh and
    // not only for the catalog above.
    //
    // Two of them are named away from the `IVolume` obligations
    // (`geometry.concepts.plato`) on purpose: `PolygonMesh3D` is a combinatorial
    // boundary that may be open or non-convex, so it does not claim to be a solid
    // with a volume — `EnclosedVolume` and `TotalFaceArea` are readings that
    // happen to coincide with those obligations when the mesh IS closed and
    // outward-wound, and are meaningless when it is not.

    // The area of one face: the magnitude of its Newell vector area
    // (`polygons.library.plato`). Exact for a planar face and the least-squares
    // reading of a nearly planar one, which is the same bargain `FaceUnitNormal`
    // makes.
    FaceArea(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Number
        => self.FacePositions(face).VectorArea.Magnitude;

    // Every face area, in face order.
    FaceAreas(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<Number>
        => self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => self.FaceArea(f));

    // The total boundary area. Coincides with the `SurfaceArea` obligation when
    // the mesh is a closed solid's boundary.
    TotalFaceArea(self: PolygonMesh3D): Number
        => SumOf(self.FaceAreas);

    // The signed volume the faces enclose, by the divergence theorem: one third
    // of the sum over faces of centroid . vectorArea
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divergence_theorem). Positive for a closed
    // mesh wound counter-clockwise seen from outside; a negative reading means
    // the winding is inverted, and a reading near zero on a mesh with faces means
    // it is not closed.
    EnclosedVolume(self: PolygonMesh3D): Number
        => SumOf(self.FaceCount.MapRange(f =>
            self.FaceCentroid(f).PositionVector.Dot(self.FacePositions(f).VectorArea))) / 3.0;

    // The length of the edge a corner directs: from its own vertex to the next
    // corner's.
    CornerEdgeLength(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Number
        => self.CornerPosition(corner).Distance(self.CornerPosition(self.NextCorner(corner)));

    // Every undirected edge's length, in edge-index order — folded over the
    // corners keeping the canonical half of each twin pair, exactly as
    // `UndirectedEdgeMidpoints` does. `Repeat(0, …)` is the empty seed.
    UndirectedEdgeLengths(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<Number>
        => self.CornerCount
            .MapRange(c => CornerIndex(c))
            .Reduce(Repeat(0, 0.0),
                (acc, c) => self.IsCanonicalCorner(c) ? acc.Append(self.CornerEdgeLength(c)) : acc);

    // The longest edge divided by the shortest: one for a solid with all edges
    // equal, which is what the uniformity constants of the expand and snub
    // catalog entries above are chosen to achieve. Undefined (division by zero)
    // on a mesh with a degenerate edge.
    EdgeLengthRatio(self: PolygonMesh3D): Number
    {
        var lengths = self.UndirectedEdgeLengths;
        var longest = lengths.Reduce(0.0, (acc, len) => acc.Max(len));
        var shortest = lengths.Reduce(longest, (acc, len) => acc.Min(len));
        return longest / shortest;
    }
```
